title: I Used the Parking-Garage Lost-Ticket Fee on the Attendant's Own Car

parts.text: I lost a ticket in a coat pocket and paid the lost-ticket maximum of forty-eight dollars at 6:20 p.m. The attendant, Rico, smirked. "Should've kept it." I was thirty-three, downtown, holding a coat that had eaten the stub. Ten minutes later I saw Rico pull out in a sedan with no ticket on the dash, waving at himself in the booth camera, gate open. The policy on the window said every vehicle needs a ticket or the maximum. I photographed his plate, the empty dash, and the window. Then the night supervisor walked over to ask why the gate was held open for a private car.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The supervisor is watching the gate he held for himself after charging me the max.

social.video_title: He billed me the lost-ticket max and waved himself out — Part 1/2
social.description: Coat pocket, forty-eight dollars, a smirk, then a sedan with no stub. Would you have eaten the fee?

parts.text: I showed the photos. Rico said staff parking was different. The window did not say that. The supervisor charged the staff lot policy, which still required a hangtag Rico did not have. He wrote Rico up. I did not get my forty-eight back because I had actually lost a ticket. I got a voucher for a future day, which is not justice, but it is accounting. I keep stubs in my wallet now. Rico uses a hangtag. The gate closes between cars like a gate.

social.video_title: Staff parking still needed a hangtag he did not have — Part 2/2
social.description: Write-up, voucher, wallet stubs. Was a smirk a hangtag?
